questions.q: In the lab scenario, what's the strongest business argument for moving 2,000 users from local authentication to SSO against the existing Okta tenant?
options: SSO makes ServiceNow load pages faster
Offboarding becomes a single Okta action instead of a separate ServiceNow-specific step for every departing employee
It eliminates the need for any roles or groups in ServiceNow
It removes the need for ServiceNow to have a sys_user table at all
questions.explain: At 2,000 users, the offboarding risk reduction — one action at Okta instead of a separate step per application — is the argument that lands hardest with a non-technical stakeholder.

questions.q: Where do the entity ID, SSO endpoint URL, and signing certificate needed for the Multi-Provider SSO record come from in this scenario?
options: They are generated automatically inside ServiceNow
From the company's Okta tenant — someone with Okta admin access must retrieve and hand them over
From each individual user's sys_user record
They aren't needed if the company already uses Okta for other apps
questions.explain: This is a real cross-team dependency: the IdP's metadata must come from Okta admin access before the ServiceNow-side configuration record can be completed.

questions.q: After this migration, what happens to the 2,000 users' existing role and group assignments in sys_user?
options: They are wiped and need to be rebuilt from scratch
They stay exactly as they were — this migration changes authentication, not authorization
They are automatically replaced by Okta group mappings
Only admin-level roles survive the migration
questions.explain: Switching from local authentication to SSO changes who verifies identity, not what roles, groups, or ACLs a user has once logged in.

questions.q: Leadership asks for MFA to be enforced as part of this migration. What's the correct action?
options: Search for a native ServiceNow MFA configuration screen and enable it there
Confirm Okta's own MFA policy is turned on and applies to the Okta application tied to this ServiceNow integration
Ignore the request since MFA isn't possible with SSO
Build a custom script in ServiceNow to prompt for a second factor
questions.explain: Since Okta is the enterprise identity chokepoint, MFA enforcement belongs at Okta — the correct step is confirming that policy, not building anything inside ServiceNow.

questions.q: Leadership then asks for different MFA rules per department. How should that request be handled in this scope?
options: Build a ServiceNow business rule to vary MFA by department
Name it clearly as an Okta policy question, outside what the ServiceNow authentication layer controls
Say it's technically impossible under any configuration
Treat it as a field-level ACL design problem
questions.explain: Per-department MFA rules are a legitimate request, but they belong to the IdP's own policy configuration — recognizing that scope boundary matters more than inventing a ServiceNow-side workaround.
